entries.4d2bdbcaa7be2e5a: Profit attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥160,992 million, up from ¥112,740 million in the previous year. Because the consolidated financial statements are prepared under [[term:ifrs|International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)]], the name of this profit differs from Japanese GAAP's 'net income attributable to owners of the parent'. The company is advancing a business portfolio reform, positioning the aircraft engine and rocket fields as growth businesses and the clean energy field as a business to be nurtured, and plans to shift management resources to those fields.

entries.699538ffeb260822: From fiscal 2026, the company states that it will shift to a stage of dramatic growth toward realizing its 'medium- to long-term direction' formulated for 2040. It will focus on three business domains (aerospace, energy and infrastructure) and will continue bold resource shifts and allocations, particularly to aerospace and clean energy. It says the traditional energy field and the industrial and social infrastructure fields will be expanded as a stable revenue base centered on life-cycle business. The three years from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028 are positioned as a period focused on upfront investment and strengthening the financial base (Phase 1).

entries.6f3e1bbf87d407ef: This field covers defense equipment systems. Amid continued heightened geopolitical risks, and against the backdrop of policies to strengthen defense capabilities, the company continues to respond to orders for large projects. Revenue increased due to expansion of the defense business. Revenue for this field alone is not printed in the securities report, but revenue from the Ministry of Defense was ¥185,784 million (¥137,627 million in the previous year); because its monetary significance increased, it has been presented as a major customer since the fiscal year ended March 2026.

entries.713697d61aafd7ca: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,643,402 million, up 1.0% from ¥1,626,831 million in the previous year. Revenue from external customers was highest in Aerospace, Space and Defense at ¥648,135 million, followed by Industrial Systems and General-Purpose Machinery at ¥438,896 million, Resources, Energy and Environment at ¥373,475 million, Social Infrastructure at ¥129,642 million, and Others at ¥53,254 million. The company explained that revenue increased, despite declines from business transfers and the reversal of progress on large projects in the previous year, due to expansion of the defense business and civil aircraft engines, as well as growing demand and improved selling prices for vehicle turbochargers.

entries.b03bd27bc9850e91: This business manufactures, sells and provides services for aircraft engines, rocket systems and space utilization, and defense equipment systems. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥648,135 million (¥552,700 million in the previous year), the largest of the four reportable segments. Major customers are the Japan Aircraft Engine Association (General Incorporated Foundation), with revenue of ¥332,088 million, and the Ministry of Defense, with revenue of ¥185,784 million. Revenue increased due to higher sales of spare parts for commercial aircraft engines and expansion of the defense business. Space equipment and flight vehicles are manufactured, sold and repaired by IHI Aerospace Co., Ltd. In February 2026, the company transferred all shares of Meisei Electric Co., Ltd., which had handled weather, disaster prevention and space businesses in this segment.

Revenue decreased, although prime movers recorded higher revenue from nuclear expansion and higher sales of medium-sized models, due to the reversal of progress on large projects in the previous year for EPC projects at Asian bases and for carbon solutions, among other factors.

entries.d082c81a528a35ee: The company says its business model, built over a long period, runs a cycle of creating overwhelmingly strong technology and creating markets with high entry barriers, and expands and extends the business through globalization and dual-use (military and civilian) applications. Also, through expansion of the life-cycle business, the company says it creates value from the perspectives of 'automation and labor saving' and 'CO₂ reduction', which it links to securing a stable revenue base.

entries.d8c9ca834fb55918: This field manufactures and sells aircraft engines and also provides maintenance and other services. For commercial aircraft engines, the aftermarket business is expanding, driven by increased operating hours, among other factors. For PW1100G-JM engines already shipped, there is an additional inspection program, and the company is working with program partners to strengthen maintenance capacity. IHI Aero Engines US Co.,Ltd. invests in commercial aircraft engine programs, and GE Passport, LLC, an equity-method affiliate, provides services for the GE Passport20 engine, including manufacturing, sales, maintenance and parts supply. Revenue for this field alone is not printed in the securities report.

entries.eb64418fce009df3: Aerospace, Space and Defense covers aircraft engines, rocket systems and space utilization, and defense equipment systems; Industrial Systems and General-Purpose Machinery covers vehicle turbochargers, parking systems, rotating machinery, heat and surface treatment, and logistics and industrial systems; Resources, Energy and Environment covers prime movers, carbon solutions and nuclear equipment; and Social Infrastructure covers bridges, sluice gates and shield systems. The company manufactures and sells these products and also provides services. The Material Handling Machinery Business was transferred to Tadano on July 1, 2025, the main affiliate of the Concrete Building Materials Business was transferred to Beltex Corporation on October 1, 2025, and the main affiliate of the Transportation Systems Business was transferred to Jei Kei Efu on December 30, 2025, respectively.
